items.text: latest `klt drc` JSON report: `status: clean`, fresh, with the deck identified (content hash). Known deck coverage gaps (rule-free layers, skipped rules) must be enumerated in the claim, not hidden behind "clean" — a clean verdict from a deck with undisclosed holes is a false claim. The report already states its own gaps, so the disclosure is those fields quoted from the cited envelope's `coverage` block (`docs/cli/drc.md`), not prose written from memory: `coverage.layers_in_stream_without_rules` (layers drawn in this stream that the deck has no rule for), `coverage.rules_skipped` (rules the deck carries but this run did not evaluate), and `coverage.deck_scope` (which chapters of the foundry DRM the deck transcribes at all). A claim that leaves a non-empty `layers_in_stream_without_rules` or `rules_skipped` unstated, or that never states the `deck_scope` its "clean" was measured inside, has not satisfied this item however clean the `status` is. **This disclosure is claimant-enforced, not tool-enforced**: `klt signoff` grades item 3 on `status: "clean"` alone — a deck with rule-free drawn layers or skipped rules grades `met` exactly like a fully-covering one. Since #2002 it does *report* all three fields (item 3's citation carries a `coverage` block quoting them verbatim, `docs/cli/signoff.md` → "DRC coverage is reported, not graded"), so a reviewer no longer has to re-open the DRC envelope to find them — but reporting is not enforcing: nothing compares them against what the claim actually disclosed, so a `met` verdict from `klt signoff` is still not evidence that the gaps were disclosed. A reviewer must read the reported `coverage` against the claim themselves. **Opt-in exception (#5789)**: a manifest that sets `require_coverage_disclosure: true` and enumerates its gaps on item 3's evidence entry (`coverage_disclosed`) has the comparison graded — a declaration that is not set-equal to the reported coverage renders the item `unmet` / `coverage_undisclosed`. The default remains claimant-enforced; the tool-enforced form is something a project opts into per manifest. **Disclosed exception for unmodified foundry cells** (operator ruling 2026-10-28): DRC violations inside an unmodified foundry-library cell (a stock I/O pad, a foundry SRAM macro) do not block `met`, provided all three of these hold: (1) the same violations — same rules, same counts — reproduce when the unmodified PDK cell is checked alone, with none of the block's own geometry; (2) the exception is pinned to the stock cell by content hash and names its rules and counts, and lapses if the cell or the counts change; (3) the T1 claim lists every such exception, and says nothing about the internals of those cells. `klt signoff` grades this from a `foundry_cell_exceptions` list on the item 3 evidence entry (`docs/cli/signoff.md` → "Foundry-cell DRC exceptions") and lists each applied exception in item 3's citation.

items.text: latest LVS report (or, per cell, a list of reports — all must pass) `status: match`, fresh, engine named, checked against the netlist from item 1 (schematic netlist for analog, synthesized/routed gate-level netlist for digital), **and that same report's `power_connectivity.status` not `"mismatch"`**. Those are two verdicts, not one: `klt lvs`'s top-level `status` is the *signal*- connectivity compare's own result, and since issue #1952 the power/ground half is reported beside it in its own `power_connectivity` block (`docs/cli/lvs.md` → "Power/ground connectivity"). `klt signoff` already grades this item on both — an `lvs`-kind check passes only on `status == "match"` **and** `power_connectivity.status != "mismatch"` (issue #1965) — so a claim resting on `status: match` alone is weaker than the tool that grades it. What the check verifies is per-standard-cell-instance *pin-to-net* correctness: on every abstracted instance, each pin the PDK library declares power/ground must reach the net the caller declared (`options.power_connectivity.expected_nets`) or, absent a declaration, the same net every other instance's same-named pin reaches; a disagreement renders `power.inconsistent_pin_net` / `power.unexpected_pin_net`, and a pin on no net at all renders `power.unconnected_pin`. **The check's reach is narrower than "the power grid is verified", and a claim must not say otherwise.** A `power_connectivity.status` of `"unchecked"` — every `reference.form` other than `gate-level-verilog`, an explicit `options.power_connectivity: false`, or a layout whose instances declare no PG pins at all — means the question was never asked; this item and `klt signoff` both read it as "does not apply here", never as "verified", so a fleet policy of "re-run LVS, look for `match`" is not by itself power-connectivity evidence (#1985). A fourth `unchecked` case existed on the route that document itself steers routed digital blocks through — `gate-level-verilog` **on a FinFET deck** (issue #4462), where the stub-form pin-to-net check does not apply. Since issue #5757 that route no longer stops at `unchecked`: after the compare, the verdict is *derived* from the expanded-cell compare — `"match"` when the compare matched and a requested supply net (`options.supply_nets`, the same allowlist that scopes supply-fragmentation findings) is proven on a matched `net_correspondence` row, with the `reason` naming the derivation and exactly the supplies the compare proved — and stays `"unchecked"` when the compare mismatched, the check was opted out, the allowlist is empty (`options.supply_nets: []` proves nothing), or no requested supply net pairs (a reference whose expanded rails float on internal nets under other names proves nothing about the top-level grid). A derived `"match"` is this item's `"match"` for every purpose below, including item 11's requirement. And even where it does run it is *not* a geometric rail/grid continuity check: whether a rail is an unbroken annulus, and whether the grid carries the current, stay `klt ring-check`, `klt power`, and the DRC deck's business — see "Power/IR-drop + EM evidence" below for what is and is not covered. Warnings-only mismatches must be listed with the claim. A second, independent engine's concurring verdict (#343) strengthens this from "one toolchain agrees with itself" to a cross-checked result. **PDK-runset path (issue #2870, operator ruling of 2026-10-08).** For device families the PDK's own open KLayout LVS runset recognises and the curated extraction deck does not, a `klt lvs` report with `"engine": "klayout-runset"` is accepted evidence for this item, on four conditions: (1) the runset is the PDK's own at a pinned revision — `klt signoff` checks `provenance.runset.content_hash` against a signoff-side allowlist (`signoff_runset.PINNED_RUNSETS`, hash → PDK revision), not against a field the block declares, and the runset file named by the report must still re-hash to that value; (2) the report is a `klt` envelope with the same `--check` re-hash guarantees as a curated-deck report (layout hash, reference netlist hash, plus the runset hash); (3) the report names its engine, and `klt signoff` carries `engine` and the runset hash distinctly in the check detail and the `met` citation; (4) every device is recognised — a `device_census` whose per-class layout and reference counts differ (compared case-insensitively; issue #6902), a report without the reference-source device evidence (`device_census.reference_source`, emitted by `klt lvs` since #6902 — a pre-#6902 report fails closed), or a source class with too few converted devices after accounting for documented runset renames on the affected cards, is a failure (`runset_unrecognised_device`), never a warning, even when `status` reads `match`. Classes the runset declares with zero instances anywhere are not graded — `coverage.declared_not_recognized` is disclosure only (issue #6902: no real block instantiates every class a PDK runset declares; the 2026-10-08 ruling itself — every device recognised, nothing dropped — is unchanged). A report from a runset that is not in the allowlist is refused `runset_not_pinned`; one whose runset file changed since the run, `runset_hash_mismatch`. **This does not change** the default: curated decks stay the route wherever they recognise every device in the block, and a block may not choose the runset to avoid a curated-deck finding. The allowlist (`signoff_runset.PINNED_RUNSETS`, listed by `klt signoff --describe-grader` under `pinned_runsets`) holds the SG13G2, SG13CMOS5L, gf180mcu and sky130 `*.lvs` runsets as of 2026-11-21. **Adding an entry** is a reviewed trust decision, never a copy of a hash from a report: fetch the PDK's runset file from its upstream repo at a named commit, `sha256` it (the same digest `_provenance.sha256_file` records), and add one entry recording `pdk`, `revision`, `repo`, `commit`, `path` and `reviewed_by`. The digest covers the top-level runset file only, so the `commit` is what fixes the `rule_decks/` it includes. A PDK whose runset cannot be fetched or run at a verifiable commit is left unpinned.

A spec needing several testbenches cites several `klt sim` envelopes, optionally naming the rows each covers and declaring the full row set; the item is met only when every cited envelope passes and every declared row is covered, and rows no envelope can express are declared gaps that keep it unmet. A row defined by an analytical/linear-model run may instead cite a committed `model-run` envelope (same per-row coverage rule: a passing measurement with a recognised, non-null `min`/`max` bound; `klt` does not execute the model).

items.title: Statistical claims carry Monte Carlo evidence
items.partition_boundary: transistor-level cells (sg13g2_inv_1, sg13g2_inv_2, sg13g2_inv_4, sg13g2_nand2_1): SPICE characterization, klt sim corner evidence and layout DRC/LVS
items.text: any accuracy, offset, or matching spec row is statistical; a corner matrix (or STA corner sweep) cannot validate it. This applies to whichever spec rows are actually statistical, regardless of block kind — most digital spec rows (functional correctness, Fmax, timing closure) are not, and a block whose spec has no statistical row must say so explicitly rather than omit the item. Where it does apply, MC runs need a recorded seed, sample count, a deterministic negative control, and results combined with (not instead of) process corners (#344). A `klt yield` JSON report — a yield estimate with its confidence interval, sample-size verdict, and Cpk/sigma-to-spec against the row's own limits — is the machine-checkable evidence for this item (`klt signoff`'s tier-verdict mode grades it the same way it grades the deterministic items above). **The campaign's own self-report is a grading input, not just a footnote** (issue #2467): a cited report whose `sample_size.verdict` is `insufficient` on any measurement renders `unmet` with `reason: "undersized_sample"`, and one whose declared negative control did not show the seeded degradation renders `unmet` with `reason: "negative_control_not_detected"` — the report's passing `status` answers only "did every declared `target_yield` hold", which a campaign declaring none can never fail. A campaign that declared **no** negative control at all is still `met`, but says so: `citation.yield_campaign.negative_control` reads `"not_declared"`, since `klt yield` itself treats that as a warning rather than a failure and whether it is acceptable for a given spec row is the claimant's call. See [`cli/signoff.md`](cli/signoff.md)'s "Campaign discipline on item 6". **This item's evidence verb needs the `yield` extra.** Unlike every other T1 item's evidence verb (`drc`, `lvs`, `extract`, `sim`, `pex`, `sta`, `functional-verification`, `erc`, `place-and-route`), `klt yield` requires the `klt_yield_native` Rust extension: install it with the `[yield]` extra (`pip install 'klayout-tools[yield]'`). As of 2026-11-06 the prebuilt `klt-yield-native` 0.1.0 wheel (Linux x86_64, macOS arm64) is on PyPI and the extra resolves for klayout-tools 0.9.1 and later. A bare `pip install klayout-tools` and the git-pinned form do not include it. A consumer on another platform (Linux aarch64, Windows, Intel macOS) needs a repo checkout with a Rust toolchain; see `docs/cli/yield.md`'s "What the extra does and does not reach" callout and `docs/releasing-native.md`. **When "not applicable" is legitimate** (issue #2865): a block whose ratified spec has *no* statistical row passes this item by a recorded "not applicable", not by a waiver at grant time and not by inventing a statistical claim. That holds only when the spec is ratified, a committed statement accounts for every spec row with the reason its row class is not statistical (for example "timing rows are corner-bounded by STA at the PDK's characterised corners"), and both are bound by content hash so editing either invalidates the claim. Any accuracy, offset, matching or yield row is statistical by definition: a spec carrying one — or a sigma, yield, Cpk or `3σ`-style bound — cannot use the outcome and needs `klt yield` evidence for that row. The outcome is available to a digital partition only; an analog partition (including the analog half of a mixed-signal block) always requires Monte Carlo evidence. `klt signoff` reports it as `not_applicable`, never as `met`. For a mixed-signal block sharing one ratified spec, `spec_rows."6.digital"` scopes this statement and scan to the digital rows. Every spec row must be assigned under `6.digital` or `6.analog`. A statistical row assigned to the digital partition still prevents this outcome. Analog rows are graded independently against their yield evidence. **Analog partitions** (issue #4183, operator ruling 2026-10-28): this restriction is intentional. Analog performance is inherently statistical (offset, mismatch, bias spread), so an analog spec with no statistical row is a gap in the spec, not a block with no variation; the grader is not relaxed and there is no analog-keyed `not_applicable` form. A mixed-signal block's analog partition that uses `not_applicable` renders `unmet` with `reason: not_applicable_wrong_partition`, even when the statement covers every spec row. It discharges item 6 one of two ways:
notes: **Add the missing statistical row(s)** to the block's spec through a decision record the operator ratifies, then supply Monte Carlo evidence (`klt yield`) for them. Where the PDK has no mismatch models, assumed mismatch is acceptable, labelled as such in the evidence.

**Declare item 6 a gap** for the analog partition. The digital partition of the same block may still use `not_applicable`. **Declared gaps keep blocking T1** (issue #5858, operator ruling 2026-11-17): a settled, hash-justified gap does *not* satisfy the roll-up, on any item or partition. `_T1_SATISFIED_STATUSES` is not widened and ruling #4183 above is untouched, so `tier: "T1"` still means every *applicable* row is evidenced. A gap is not a permanent state: a row that cannot be evidenced today is a statement about today's tools and inputs, and a request to build what is missing, either a klayout-tools feature or a new EDA project. A declared gap therefore names the open issue that would close it, and a gap with no such link is a signoff finding. A row that is unevidenceable for a reason no tool could ever fix is a different case, closer to `not_applicable`, and goes back to the operator rather than being declared a gap. The hash-justified declaration and the separate count and listing of declared gaps belong to #5599. **Several statistical rows, only some evidenced** (issue #2908): item 6 is a claim about *every* statistical row, so a manifest may declare the row set under `spec_rows."6"` and cite one `klt yield` report per row set (`rows` on each citation). Item 6 grades `met` only when every declared row is covered by a passing citation against a ratified target. A row with no citation (`uncovered_rows`), a row declared a `gap` (`declared_gaps` — pending work that a named issue should close, never a permanent pass; issue #5599 adds a justified form carrying a hash-bound rationale artifact and the issue that would close the gap, and an operator ruling on #5858, 2026-11-17 settled that a gap keeps blocking T1), or a row declared `ratified: false` (`unratified_rows`, evidence against a proposed limit is provisional) grades `unmet` / `partial_coverage`, never `met`. Without a declaration the item grades as before; a `not_applicable` entry contradicts a declared row set and is `invalid_evidence`.

items.partition_boundary: add8 synthesis/place-and-route benchmark flow on the stock sg13g2_stdcell baseline
items.text: any accuracy, offset, or matching spec row is statistical; a corner matrix (or STA corner sweep) cannot validate it. This applies to whichever spec rows are actually statistical, regardless of block kind — most digital spec rows (functional correctness, Fmax, timing closure) are not, and a block whose spec has no statistical row must say so explicitly rather than omit the item. Where it does apply, MC runs need a recorded seed, sample count, a deterministic negative control, and results combined with (not instead of) process corners (#344). A `klt yield` JSON report — a yield estimate with its confidence interval, sample-size verdict, and Cpk/sigma-to-spec against the row's own limits — is the machine-checkable evidence for this item (`klt signoff`'s tier-verdict mode grades it the same way it grades the deterministic items above). **The campaign's own self-report is a grading input, not just a footnote** (issue #2467): a cited report whose `sample_size.verdict` is `insufficient` on any measurement renders `unmet` with `reason: "undersized_sample"`, and one whose declared negative control did not show the seeded degradation renders `unmet` with `reason: "negative_control_not_detected"` — the report's passing `status` answers only "did every declared `target_yield` hold", which a campaign declaring none can never fail. A campaign that declared **no** negative control at all is still `met`, but says so: `citation.yield_campaign.negative_control` reads `"not_declared"`, since `klt yield` itself treats that as a warning rather than a failure and whether it is acceptable for a given spec row is the claimant's call. See [`cli/signoff.md`](cli/signoff.md)'s "Campaign discipline on item 6". **This item's evidence verb needs the `yield` extra.** Unlike every other T1 item's evidence verb (`drc`, `lvs`, `extract`, `sim`, `pex`, `sta`, `functional-verification`, `erc`, `place-and-route`), `klt yield` requires the `klt_yield_native` Rust extension: install it with the `[yield]` extra (`pip install 'klayout-tools[yield]'`). As of 2026-11-06 the prebuilt `klt-yield-native` 0.1.0 wheel (Linux x86_64, macOS arm64) is on PyPI and the extra resolves for klayout-tools 0.9.1 and later. A bare `pip install klayout-tools` and the git-pinned form do not include it. A consumer on another platform (Linux aarch64, Windows, Intel macOS) needs a repo checkout with a Rust toolchain; see `docs/cli/yield.md`'s "What the extra does and does not reach" callout and `docs/releasing-native.md`. **When "not applicable" is legitimate** (issue #2865): a block whose ratified spec has *no* statistical row passes this item by a recorded "not applicable", not by a waiver at grant time and not by inventing a statistical claim. That holds only when the spec is ratified, a committed statement accounts for every spec row with the reason its row class is not statistical (for example "timing rows are corner-bounded by STA at the PDK's characterised corners"), and both are bound by content hash so editing either invalidates the claim. Any accuracy, offset, matching or yield row is statistical by definition: a spec carrying one — or a sigma, yield, Cpk or `3σ`-style bound — cannot use the outcome and needs `klt yield` evidence for that row. The outcome is available to a digital partition only; an analog partition (including the analog half of a mixed-signal block) always requires Monte Carlo evidence. `klt signoff` reports it as `not_applicable`, never as `met`. For a mixed-signal block sharing one ratified spec, `spec_rows."6.digital"` scopes this statement and scan to the digital rows. Every spec row must be assigned under `6.digital` or `6.analog`. A statistical row assigned to the digital partition still prevents this outcome. Analog rows are graded independently against their yield evidence. **Analog partitions** (issue #4183, operator ruling 2026-10-28): this restriction is intentional. Analog performance is inherently statistical (offset, mismatch, bias spread), so an analog spec with no statistical row is a gap in the spec, not a block with no variation; the grader is not relaxed and there is no analog-keyed `not_applicable` form. A mixed-signal block's analog partition that uses `not_applicable` renders `unmet` with `reason: not_applicable_wrong_partition`, even when the statement covers every spec row. It discharges item 6 one of two ways:
notes: **Add the missing statistical row(s)** to the block's spec through a decision record the operator ratifies, then supply Monte Carlo evidence (`klt yield`) for them. Where the PDK has no mismatch models, assumed mismatch is acceptable, labelled as such in the evidence.

**Declare item 6 a gap** for the analog partition. The digital partition of the same block may still use `not_applicable`. **Declared gaps keep blocking T1** (issue #5858, operator ruling 2026-11-17): a settled, hash-justified gap does *not* satisfy the roll-up, on any item or partition. `_T1_SATISFIED_STATUSES` is not widened and ruling #4183 above is untouched, so `tier: "T1"` still means every *applicable* row is evidenced. A gap is not a permanent state: a row that cannot be evidenced today is a statement about today's tools and inputs, and a request to build what is missing, either a klayout-tools feature or a new EDA project. A declared gap therefore names the open issue that would close it, and a gap with no such link is a signoff finding. A row that is unevidenceable for a reason no tool could ever fix is a different case, closer to `not_applicable`, and goes back to the operator rather than being declared a gap. The hash-justified declaration and the separate count and listing of declared gaps belong to #5599. **Several statistical rows, only some evidenced** (issue #2908): item 6 is a claim about *every* statistical row, so a manifest may declare the row set under `spec_rows."6"` and cite one `klt yield` report per row set (`rows` on each citation). Item 6 grades `met` only when every declared row is covered by a passing citation against a ratified target. A row with no citation (`uncovered_rows`), a row declared a `gap` (`declared_gaps` — pending work that a named issue should close, never a permanent pass; issue #5599 adds a justified form carrying a hash-bound rationale artifact and the issue that would close the gap, and an operator ruling on #5858, 2026-11-17 settled that a gap keeps blocking T1), or a row declared `ratified: false` (`unratified_rows`, evidence against a proposed limit is provisional) grades `unmet` / `partial_coverage`, never `met`. Without a declaration the item grades as before; a `not_applicable` entry contradicts a declared row set and is `invalid_evidence`.

rows.reason: The row height is a fixed layout dimension of 3.36 um (8 tracks).
The routing grid specifies a fixed pitch of 0.42 um on each axis.
Layer inspection determines whether all intra-cell routing uses Metal1.
Each pin location is checked against the specified routing grid.
Counting the combinational cells in the library determines whether it reaches the target or stretch count.
The target excludes sequential cells and the stretch specifies a count of eight.
The DRC verdict depends on whether the SG13G2 deck reports a violation on the given layout.
LVS compares the extracted layout netlist with the schematic and returns a match verdict.
The Liberty views are required at named process, voltage and temperature points, with TT at target and FF and SS added at stretch.
The area bound compares post-synthesis cell area for add8 mapped with each library under the same flow and constraints.
The energy bound compares total post-synthesis energy over one fixed seeded vector set at TT, using the same clock period and power tool for both libraries.
The period bound compares worst input-to-output path delays at each specified corner using the same virtual clock and I/O constraints for both post-synthesis netlists.

items.text: the spec suite re-run against the netlist extracted from the layout, not only the drawn schematic (#252). Parasitic extraction has landed (#217, `klt extract --parasitics`); a `klt pex` report's `extraction.model` field is the machine-checkable statement of what the extracted netlist's lumped-RC model does and does not account for (quasi-static, vertical-overlap coupling only, issue #760 — see `docs/cli/pex.md` → "Top-level fields"). A `klt pex` JSON report — the per-corner, per-spec-row schematic-vs-extracted delta — is the machine-checkable evidence for this item, and the *only* evidence `klt signoff`'s tier-verdict mode accepts for it: unlike every other item, item 7 rejects a passing citation of any other kind, since a clean DRC or a pre-layout schematic sim proves nothing about post-layout behaviour (#871). `klt pex` (Epic #709, issue #801) is implemented — see `docs/cli/pex.md` for its full contract and `docs/cli/signoff.md`'s "Item 7 is kind-restricted" section for how `klt signoff` binds to it. Epic #709 Phase 1c (#803) is the first end-to-end proof of this item on a real analog canary (`blocks/sky130-ota-5t` / `examples/design-pipeline/`, see that directory's README "S10 pex delta proof" section) — every `delta[]` row is explainable directly from the extracted netlist's own added R/C, not merely reported, including the (measured, not assumed) no-degradation rows that canary's current topology produces. notes: A `klt pex` citation is only as good as the **device-body bias** of the netlist it ran on (#1983). A device body left on an anonymous, deck-synthesized net has no DC bias path at all, which makes a resimulation of that extracted netlist *physically wrong, not merely imprecise* (`docs/cli/extract.md` → "Coverage") — the run converges and reports numbers, and those numbers are not comparable to the schematic leg they are being diffed against. A `klt pex` report states the condition in its own `body_bias` block (`docs/cli/pex.md`), and `klt signoff` surfaces it verbatim on this item's citation (`citation.body_bias`). **It does not grade on it**: an item-7 citation whose `body_bias.status` is `"unbiased"` still renders `met`, because the condition is a deck-coverage property some PDKs produce on every layout they extract, not a defect this command can adjudicate. So a claim citing item 7 must read that field and state whether its post-layout numbers were measured on a properly-biased netlist — claimant-enforced, exactly like item 3's DRC-coverage disclosure. The same discipline applies upstream at item 4: `klt lvs`'s `body_verification` block says whether the compare verified the body ties at all, and `"unchecked"` (a pre-extracted netlist) is not `"verified"`.

items.partition_boundary: transistor-level cells (sg13g2_inv_1, sg13g2_inv_2, sg13g2_inv_4, sg13g2_nand2_1): SPICE characterization, klt sim corner evidence and layout DRC/LVS
items.text: the `klt erc` supply evidence below, plus an LVS report (item 4's own) whose reference actually carried the supply nets, so the supplies were part of the compare rather than absent from it: every declared supply net appears in that report's `net_correspondence` paired to a reference-side net. A SPICE reference satisfies this by construction; a signal-only `gate-level-verilog` reference does not, which is why the Digital column asks for `power_connectivity` instead. **That pairing check is not independent of the compare's own verdict** (issue #2495), and a claimant should read it as a participation test, not as a second opinion. `net_correspondence` lists only the nets the comparer *matched*, so for a SPICE reference — which declares its supplies by construction — "every declared supply appears paired" is implied by any `match` and destroyed by any `mismatch`, including one with no bearing on a rail: a restated device parameter or a moved signal-net connection collapses the pairing along with everything else. This item's LVS half is therefore **gated on item 4 passing**: an analog block cannot reach `met` here while its compare is mismatched, however complete its `klt erc` supply evidence is, because no reading of a mismatched compare can say the supplies took part in it. What the report does distinguish is *which half* is missing — `klt signoff` renders `lvs_did_not_pass` (not the plain `check_failed`) when the ERC supply evidence is complete and continuous and only the LVS half is unavailable, naming in `detail.power_delivery` the supplies the ERC run did prove. A set citing only the `erc` or only the `lvs` part renders `power_delivery_parts_missing` (not `wrong_kind`), naming the absent part and crediting the supplies a resolved ERC spec proved. Produce the ERC supply spec anyway — it is the half that survives an unrelated LVS defect, and it is what makes the distinction visible. A `klayout-runset` report (item 4's PDK-runset path) can be this LVS half under the same pin and re-hash conditions: the engine lists the nets its compare paired in `net_correspondence` (issue #2870), so the supply-pairing test above reads the same way, with the same "participation test, not a second opinion" caveat. An unpinned or modified runset renders `runset_not_pinned` / `runset_hash_mismatch` here too.
notes: Both columns rest on the same `klt erc` **supply spec** run (`docs/cli/erc.md`): a spec declaring every supply as a `nets[]` entry with `"kind": "supply"`, a stackup covering the layers the supply is routed on, and the `ties[]` declarations for the well/substrate taps. Every declared supply must resolve to exactly **one** electrical island — or, when the entry declares `nets[].islands` (issue #2400), to exactly that declared count of deliberately separate domains, so a legitimately multi-domain supply (one library PG pin name on independent islands) can satisfy this item instead of being unreachable by construction — with no `erc.unconnected_net` and no `erc.supply_short` naming it. A spec whose supplies include a **deliberate tie between two names** (a sub-block port name and the assembly's name for one node) declares it with `nets[].same_net_as` (issue #2463): the tie then grades as a pass instead of a permanent `erc.supply_short`, and its *absence* — `erc.expected_short_missing` naming a declared supply — blocks this item in the short's place, so declaring the tie converts a false blocking finding into a real check rather than into no evidence. **Supplies that share a substrate body are graded too** (issue #5346): an `erc.supply_short` with `via: "substrate"` blocks this item like a metal one, and a cited run that *disclosed* the substrate path undecidable (`erc_coverage.inapplicable[erc.supply_short]`, reason `substrate_isolation_undecidable`) is `unmet` with the same-named reason and its `missing` list in `detail.power_delivery`; only an evaluated-clean run (`erc.supply_short.substrate` in `checked`) is `met`. **The severed-rail half of "exactly one island" is gradeable too, where the spec declares the roles a supply owns** (issue #2524). `erc.unconnected_net` counts islands *carrying the declared label*, so a single-label supply rail severed into a labelled piece and an unlabelled orphan grades clean (`docs/cli/erc.md` → "`erc.unconnected_net` counts labelled islands, not conductor islands") — the ordinary shape for hand-built or generated analog, where the label names a port rather than annotating every rail segment. Before this rule existed, a met item 11 on such a block rested on a negative the evidence could not actually state. A supply that declares `nets[].roles` (issue #2510) turns the measurement on, and conductor on those owned roles reachable from no label is `erc.unlabelled_conductor`, which blocks this item under the same declared-name filter `erc.unconnected_net` uses. The **negative** is what a met item now carries: `power_delivery.supply_unlabelled_islands` names each declared supply that owns its roles and that net's `nets[].unlabelled_islands` — all `0` for a met item — so a grader can see the clean verdict was measured over the whole conductor, not only over what carried a label. It is `{}` for a cited run whose supplies declared no `roles` (and for every pre-#2510 envelope): the honest "not measured", never a fabricated zero, so "checked, and it is zero" stays distinguishable from "nobody asked". **Declaring `nets[].roles` is therefore optional but strictly better evidence** — and where an owned role legitimately carries unlabelled fill or a floating shield, `nets[].unlabelled_allowed_boxes` declares that away with the carve-out echoed in `provenance.net_exclusions`, rather than forcing the role to be left unowned and the severed-rail question unasked. A grader seeing an `erc.supply_short` on a supply-sensing analog block should check the cited report's `provenance.devices` (empty, or missing the bodies on the conducting path) before reading the finding as a real short. **`--deck` (issue #2204) removes the need for hand-declaration for a device a curated extraction deck already knows about**: running the same supply-spec check with `--deck <name>` (e.g. `gf180mcu`/`sky130`) auto-carves out every deck-recognised `ResistorDevice`/`CapacitorDevice` body whose conducting-body layer matches a declared `stackup`/`vias` role, echoed in `provenance.devices` exactly as a hand-declared entry is (plus `source: "deck"`) — see `docs/cli/erc.md`'s "Deck-driven device-marker auto-detection". A run without `--deck`, or whose device is not yet covered by any curated deck's `resistors`/ `capacitors` tables, still needs the explicit `devices[]` declaration above; a grader should check `provenance.deck` alongside `provenance.devices` before treating a clean `erc.supply_short` read as covered by auto-detection rather than a hand-declaration that happens to be present.

**Port accessibility — PROVISIONAL, not yet in force** (issue #2839; operator ruling 2AMLogic/product#134, amendment text drafted in 2AMLogic/product PR #168 and awaiting the two-key ratification). Every supply the cited `klt erc` spec declares must be published as an **edge-accessible boundary port** and named in a **machine-readable abstract**: (1) a `klt socket-check` envelope whose `power_ports` facts show, for each declared supply, a `POWER`/`GROUND` pin of that name with drawn conductor under its label lying within the edge band of a counted outline edge with a clear approach channel (no other conductor on its layer between it and the edge), on an allowed layer; and (2) a `klt lef-abstract` envelope whose LEF carries a `PIN` of the same name with `USE POWER`/`USE GROUND` matching the port, a drawn `PORT` on the same layer touching the port, and a `SIZE` equal to the outline. Parameters, with their provisional defaults, are set per block in the `klt signoff` manifest's `power_ports` object: the edge band (`edge_band_um`, default `0` — the port must touch the outline; the draft proposes one minimum metal pitch), the counted edges (all four), and the allowed layers (default: any layer that resolves to a LEF routing layer, the draft's recommendation). Until ratification `klt signoff` grades this clause only for a block that opts in (`power_ports.required: true`, or port evidence cited in item 11's list), after the ERC/LVS rules above are proven, rendering `power_port_unproven`, `no_edge_power_port`, `power_port_interior_only`, `power_port_layer_disallowed`, `lef_power_pin_missing` or `lef_power_pin_mismatch` when it fails — see `docs/cli/signoff.md` → "Item 11 port accessibility". Not graded yet: one port per declared island of a multi-island supply.
